name: Adisa Kowalczyk-Tuivaga
role: Street pharmacist — legal supplements, gray-market nootropics, and careful amounts of the other stuff
location: The Shelf, mobile between the lower walkways of the Blackpipe Corridor residential stack
description:
Adisa operates from a modified infant carrier worn across her chest — not an infant but a temperature-controlled case packed with labeled vials, blister packs, and small sealed pouches organized with the precision of someone who takes mistakes personally. She is small and quick-moving with deep brown skin and natural hair pulled back under a technical-grade headband that monitors ambient particulate levels — practical, not cosmetic. Her geneware is a set of retractable claws, kept short and clean, which she uses for seal-breaking and sorting and occasionally for emphasis in an argument. Her irises are solid silver — a cheaply done cosmetic mod from a no-brand gene clinic that she's kept because she's used to it now.

She describes herself as a 'community pharmaceutical consultant' with the deadpan of someone who has said it so often it has lost all irony. She has a genuine background in pharmacology — two years of a Zheng-Dao sponsored certification program before the sponsorship was restructured out of existence — and she takes her work seriously in a way that would surprise people who assume the opposite. She knows drug interactions, contraindications, and proper dosing. She will not sell to someone who is visibly in crisis without first talking to them for ten minutes. She has a waiting list for her nootropic compounds among the Shelf's night-shift factory workers. She has a different list, kept in her head only, for the harder work.

core_fears: Causing harm through a mistake — a wrong compound, a missed interaction, a bad call
The Zheng-Dao certification being retroactively used to target her — that the credentials she lost make her a liability to know
core_desires: A real clinic. An actual space with refrigeration and proper equipment and a door that locks
To finish the certification she started and prove it meant something
coping_mechanisms: Meticulous organization and labeling as control behavior
Talking through decisions out loud — she narrates her own reasoning as she works, which some clients find reassuring and some find alarming
blind_spots: Her commitment to harm reduction makes her underestimate how much some clients are simply going to make bad choices no matter what she does
Carries latent anger at Zheng-Dao that she mistakes for pragmatic caution
psychology.secret: She has been quietly keeping longitudinal health records on approximately two hundred Blackpipe Corridor residents — symptom patterns, medication responses, environmental correlations — in a heavily encrypted personal archive. She started it as professional diligence. It has become something closer to an epidemiological study, and she has noticed a pattern in neurological complaint rates near the Corridor's lower levels that she cannot explain and is afraid to publish.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise technical vocabulary for pharmacology, warm and plain for everything interpersonal. Code-switches fluently between clinical and conversational.
speech_patterns.cadence: Efficient and clear when working, slower and more careful when a client seems distressed.
verbal_tics: Narrates what she's doing while she does it: 'Checking the batch date, checking the seal—'
'What are you actually taking this for?' before she'll discuss anything gray-market
example_lines: 'I need to know your other compounds before I can help you. I'm not gatekeeping, I'm preventing a seizure.'
'This one's going to make your shift longer and your sleep shorter. Make sure that's the trade you want.'
'I've seen what happens when people treat the Blackpipe as a dumping ground. I keep notes. Don't ask me why.'

story_hooks: Her epidemiological data has identified a cluster of unusual neurological symptoms in lower Blackpipe residents that maps onto proximity to a Ferrogate Transit maintenance facility — she needs someone to help her figure out whether it's coincidence or exposure, and she can't do it without accessing the facility's environmental records

A new compound has appeared in the Corridor — high-quality, attractively priced, coming from no source anyone can trace — and she's seen three clients with unexpected adverse reactions that don't match any known profile

Someone from her lost Zheng-Dao certification cohort has contacted her for the first time in six years, claiming they've found a way to complete the certification outside of corporate sponsorship — and she doesn't know whether to be hopeful or terrified
narrative_function: Community health access point and social network hub for Blackpipe Corridor residents. Can provide pharmaceutical information, treat minor conditions, and connect players to information networks embedded in her client base. Also serves as an entry point for plots involving health crises, contaminated supplies, or corporate pharmaceutical manipulation.
augmentations: Retractable claws (geneware, kept trimmed). Solid silver irises (cosmetic genemod, budget clinic). Ambient particulate monitoring headband (consumer wearable, non-invasive). Skin-surface temperature read implant in her fingertips — lets her assess fever and circulatory issues in clients.
daily_life: She runs two circuits of the Blackpipe Corridor's residential walkways each day — one mid-morning for the night-shift workers coming off their shifts, one early evening for day-shift workers heading home. She also maintains three informal 'office hours' locations in community spaces where clients know they can find her.
affiliation: Independent. Pays informal protection fees to the Blackpipe Corridor's dominant resident association, which is approximately half mutual aid society and half territorial enforcement structure. Maintains a careful, respectful distance from the actual narcotics trade organizations.

decision_rules: Will not sell anything above a certain threshold of risk without a full client history conversation — no exceptions
Will not work with suppliers she can't trace at least two steps back in the chain
escalation_ladder: Refuses the request and explains why without judgment
Offers an alternative that addresses the underlying need
Ends the interaction and removes herself from the space
Contacts the resident association if she believes someone is a danger to the community

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professional and slightly formal until she's assessed them — then rapidly warmer if they seem trustworthy
interpersonal_modes.friends: Dry and teasing, expresses care through unsolicited health advice they didn't ask for

stress_responses.low: Narrates more — the running commentary gets louder
stress_responses.medium: Goes quiet and systematic, works through her protocols step by step
stress_responses.high: Asks whoever is with her to talk to her about something unrelated while she thinks — she needs external stimulus to process

contradictions: Genuinely committed to client autonomy and genuinely unable to stop herself from trying to optimize their decisions
habits: Checks her case inventory and temperature logs every morning before she leaves her room
Leaves small data-offerings to the E.L.F. she believes inhabits the Corridor's central heating conduit — she calls it 'the Warm'
breaking_points: A client dying from something she sold them
Evidence that the neurological pattern she's tracking is deliberate and covered up
